title: BusinessOps Anomaly Scan
description: One anomaly scan. The schema is shaped so a deviation cannot be reported without the baseline it was measured against, and so the scan's own coverage is visible: every checked period appears in `observations`, not only the flagged ones, which is what distinguishes 'nothing was found' from 'nothing was looked at'. An anomaly is a measured deviation and nothing more — it establishes no cause, and `fraud_boundary` carries that statement in the data rather than only in prose.

sensitivity.description: Moves the detector thresholds. It never changes the arithmetic.

fraud_boundary.description: The strongest permitted statement about what an anomaly means. Emitted with every scan.

scanned_metrics.description: Per-metric coverage. A metric that could not be scanned appears here with its status rather than being omitted.

observations.description: Every period checked, flagged or not.

findings.description: The flagged observations as analytical findings. Always CALCULATION: a deviation is measured, not modelled.

baseline.description: What normal was taken to be. A deviation without its baseline is an assertion, not a finding.

deviation_pct.description: Absent when the baseline is zero, where a percentage is undefined rather than infinite.

score.description: The deviation expressed in multiples of the detector's own typical prediction error. A ratio of two measured quantities: the engine fits no distribution and tests none, so this is not a sigma, carries no probability, and implies no significance level.

status.description: normal / unusual = the detector's verdict; material_anomaly additionally cleared the user's materiality policy; insufficient_data = no baseline could be established.

materiality.description: From the existing materiality policy. Independent of `status`; only agreement produces material_anomaly.

method.description: The detector that produced this verdict. Only a detector marked as triggering may raise a flag; a corroborating detector is measured and reported but cannot flag a period alone.

contributors.description: Where the deviation sits in the data. Attribution locates it; it never explains it.

label.description: Passed through the privacy policy; pseudonymised where the presentation mode requires it.
